newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says to raise deposit rate to 2.9%.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says to raise deposit rate to 2.9%.

text.p: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Monday it will raise the interest rate it pays to other ministries for their long-term deposits by 0.3 percentage point to 2.9 percent, effective from Friday.

The move lifts the rate from a record low of 2.6 percent, and follows a rise in the coupon rate of the latest auctioned 10-year Japanese government bonds (JGBs), on which the deposit rate is customarily set.
The coupon rate for the JGB to be issued on June 20 rose to 2.7 percent from a record low 2.4 percent for the May issue.

The MOF's Trust Fund Bureau channels funds raised via deposits made by the Health Ministry and the Posts and Telecommunications Ministry to government-affiliated financial institutions and other quasi-governmental bodies through the fiscal investment and loan programme (FILP).
The programme is widely known as Japan's "second budget" for the role it plays in supplementing the state budget.
